children.title: Knowles Fire Burnover Kills Three Federal Firefighters and Injures Two
children.description_medium: On June 27, 2026, five federal wildland firefighters were caught in a burnover while making an initial attack on the Knowles Fire in western Colorado.  Three firefighters died at the scene and two were injured.  The Interior Department’s account identifies the incident as the Knowles Fire burnover, not the “Snyder Fire” named in the original card.
children.description_long: On June 27, 2026, five federal wildland firefighters were caught in a burnover while making an initial attack on the Knowles Fire in western Colorado. Three firefighters died at the scene and two were injured. The Interior Department’s account identifies the incident as the Knowles Fire burnover, not the “Snyder Fire” named in the original card. The department’s release provides the incident date and initial casualty count. An accident investigation was still underway in the supplied reporting, so the event description does not assign responsibility or connect the burnover to Forest Service staffing, prescribed-burning levels, or suppression policy. The Interior Department’s release gives the incident date and casualty chronology and says an investigation remained underway after the fourth death. Reuters’s later reporting discusses broader firefighter entrapment concerns and criticism, but it does not report a final causal finding for this particular burnover. The supplied evidence therefore supports a careful incident record and a later casualty update. It cannot establish that Forest Service staffing changes or prescribed-burn policy caused the Knowles Fire incident. Those claims need separate records and evidence before they can be described as events or connected to these deaths.
children.date_uncertainty: Event dates are identified in the supplied reporting; publication dates may be later.

children.title: Fourth Firefighter Dies From Knowles Fire Burnover Injuries
children.description_medium: Nathan Matthews died on July 24, 2026, from burns sustained in the June 27 Knowles Fire burnover in Colorado.  His death brought the incident’s death toll to four; three firefighters had died at the scene and two others were injured on June 27.  The Interior Department announced the later death and said an accident investigation remained underway.
children.description_long: Nathan Matthews died on July 24, 2026, from burns sustained in the June 27 Knowles Fire burnover in Colorado. His death brought the incident’s death toll to four; three firefighters had died at the scene and two others were injured on June 27. The Interior Department announced the later death and said an accident investigation remained underway. This is a distinct date in the casualty timeline, not a fourth death occurring on the day of the burnover.
